help.tips[0].examples[0].en: When I arrived, the train had already left.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: She had read the letter before I came back.
help.tips[0].check.whyEn: einschlafen is a change of state, so it takes sein; the earlier event goes into the Plusquamperfekt: waren eingeschlafen.
help.tips[0].en.text: ich hatte gegessen, du hattest gelesen, er hatte gekauft · ich war gegangen, sie war gekommen, wir waren gefahren. Same helper choice as the Perfekt: sein for gehen, kommen, fahren, aufstehen, einschlafen, umziehen, bleiben, sein, werden.
help.tips[0].en.title: hatte / war + Partizip II
help.tips[0].en.trap: English 'had gone' uses 'had'; German uses war gegangen. The sein-verbs keep sein in every compound tense.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: After I had moved, I quickly got to know new people.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: After we had eaten, we went for a walk.
help.tips[1].check.whyEn: The main clause is Präteritum (ging), so the nachdem-clause goes one step further back: geschrieben hatte. schreiben takes haben.
help.tips[1].en.text: Nachdem wir gegessen hatten, gingen wir spazieren. Nachdem er die Prüfung bestanden hatte, feierte er. The nachdem-clause is one step earlier, so one tense earlier.
help.tips[1].en.title: nachdem + Plusquamperfekt, main clause + Präteritum
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: I wanted to call him, but he had already switched off his phone.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: When I arrived, the train had already left.
help.tips[2].check.whyEn: bereits in a past story marks the earlier event: hatte gekauft. kaufen takes haben.
help.tips[2].en.text: Er war schon gegangen. Wir hatten bereits gegessen. When 'already' appears in a past story, the verb is usually Plusquamperfekt.
help.tips[2].en.title: schon and bereits signal it
help.tips[3].examples[1].en: I have seen the film. → I had already seen the film.
help.tips[3].check.whyEn: Only the helper moves into the past: bin becomes war. aufstehen keeps sein.
help.tips[3].en.text: Perfekt = one step back (habe gegessen). Plusquamperfekt = two steps back: the helper itself goes into the past (hatte gegessen). Count the steps.
help.tips[3].en.title: Two steps back = two past markers
help.context.en: When I came home yesterday, my sister had already arrived. She had found the key under the mat and had already made coffee. After we had talked for an hour, I realised: I had forgotten to lock the car. Luckily nothing had happened.
help.mistakes[0].whyEn: nachdem with a past main clause takes the Plusquamperfekt.
help.mistakes[2].whyEn: The earlier event needs the Plusquamperfekt.
help.hookEn: Reach one step further back in a story: Als ich ankam, war der Zug schon abgefahren, the train had already gone.
help.introEn: The Plusquamperfekt is the past before the past: when you are already telling a story in the Präteritum or Perfekt and need to reach one step further back. Als ich ankam, war der Zug schon abgefahren (when I arrived, the train had already left). Nachdem wir gegessen hatten, gingen wir spazieren. It is built exactly like the Perfekt, but with the helper in the Präteritum: hatte / war + Partizip II — hatte gegessen, war gegangen; the same haben/sein choice as in the Perfekt (movement and change of state take sein). Its natural partner is nachdem (after), which almost always takes the Plusquamperfekt in its clause and the Präteritum in the main clause, and the adverb schon (already). You need it to read narratives and to write 'nachdem'-sentences correctly. In the quiz you write both parts in their places: in a main clause the helper is in position 2 and the participle at the end (… war der Zug schon abgefahren); in a nachdem- or weil-clause the participle comes first and the helper is the very last word (Nachdem wir gegessen hatten, …).
help.rememberEn[0]: hatte / war + participle: the earlier of two past events.
sentences[0].whyEn: nachdem demands the past-before-the-past: hatte/war + participle — gegessen hatten, helper last.
sentences[1].whyEn: The earlier of two events: war … abgefahren — movement takes war.
sentences[2].whyEn: bestanden hatte — be- takes no ge-, hatte at the end.
sentences[3].whyEn: The forgetting came before: vergessen hatte.
sentences[4].whyEn: Disappearing is a change of state: war … verschwunden.
sentences[5].whyEn: Moving house takes sein: umgezogen war.
sentences[7].whyEn: Falling asleep is a change of state: waren … eingeschlafen.
sentences[8].whyEn: gearbeitet hatte — regular participle, hatte last.
sentences[11].whyEn: The reading came first: hatte … gelesen.
sentences[13].whyEn: hatten … gebucht — the booking came before the trip.
sentences[15].whyEn: verabschiedet hatten — ver- without ge-; reflexive verbs take haben.
sentences[16].whyEn: hatte … erlebt — er- takes no ge-.
